html:
SMTO-WEB-0012 — No working web search provider is available

GUID: 646ae116-2a01-418b-836b-c133ae5cf83c
Slug: provider-unavailable
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't search the web because no search provider is set up and turned on, the chosen provider can't be found, or the search server refused the connection. Nothing was searched.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Capabilities and select Configure Web. Under Search providers, make sure at least one provider is Enabled, or select Add provider to add one. SMTO can only search through a provider that exists and is turned on.
  2. Choose that provider in Default provider, or set Fallback search to something other than Off, then select Save. With no default and fallback turned off, SMTO has nowhere to send searches.
  3. Select Test connection for the provider. If it says the connection was refused and you run your own search server, start that server and test again. A refused connection means nothing is accepting searches at that address right now.

What success looks like

  • Configure Web shows Ready, Test connection shows Connected, and a new web search returns results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the search server. Don't turn off secure connection checks to get the search server to connect.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Web Search is unavailable: the requested or default provider is not in the configuration, the configuration is invalid or yields an empty provider chain, or the provider refused the connection.

What this means

  • The requested provider ID is absent, or a search connection is refused by the selected endpoint. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • The requested provider ID is absent, or a search connection is refused by the selected endpoint.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish provider lookup failure from a refused socket before editing configuration.

How to fix it

  • Check the Web Skill configuration: test_configuration in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/models.py returns provider_unavailable when the selected provider_id is absent, build_skill.search in skill.py does so for an invalid configuration or empty provider_chain (no enabled default and fallback.mode off), and SearXNGProvider.search does so on ConnectionRefusedError. Configure an enabled default or permitted fallback and confirm the endpoint is listening.
  • Inspect the configured Web provider and network and restore the service.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact selected provider exists, is enabled when required and accepts the connection.

What not to do

  • Do not invent a provider outage cause or disable connection security.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
